A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOOSE-Chem and the same 51-paper chemistry study. All 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5-6 report original retrieval, hypothesis-generation, ranking, baseline and ablation results, including expert assessments. Appendix A.7 reports agreement between expert and GPT-4o evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these experiments and adds Llama retrieval comparisons, Claude/Gemini evaluations, component analyses, ground-truth ranking results and inter-expert agreement measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed retrieval, mutation/refinement/recombination, multistep search, beam selection and four-criterion ranking procedures remain unchanged. 'Evolutionary unit' names the existing evolutionary component. Newly tested ablations do not establish a change to the full method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 51 chemistry/materials papers and retain the same retrieval, hypothesis-rediscovery and ranking tasks. TOMATO-Chem is a newly supplied benchmark name. Added model comparisons and validation analyses operate within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Llama-3.1-8B, 70B and 405B comparisons against GPT-4o for retrieval. Table 10 replaces the isolated no-mutation/recombination comparator with a joint no-multistep/no-EU variant. SciMON, MOOSE and Qi et al. remain the external framework baselines; Claude and Gemini are additional evaluators.

E3.justification: v4 adds model-scale retrieval settings, Claude/Gemini rescoring of existing hypotheses, a ground-truth ranking control and third-expert checking of 48 sampled comparison pairs. Table 10 revises the ablation controls. Table 6 also changes the stated Matched Score rubric, while Appendix A.12 retains v1's evaluation prompt; whether existing scores used the revised rubric is unresolved.

E4.justification: New analyses test evaluator robustness, model-scale sensitivity, contributions of evolutionary branches, significance feedback, ranking of published hypotheses and inter-expert agreement. Table 10 changes the component-removal comparisons. The background-option ablation and all four case studies already existed in v1 and are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added inter-expert table reuses the existing hard/soft consistency definitions, adding reliability results without introducing a different statistical estimator or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Claude/Gemini Top MS scores of 4.471/3.686, a 0.65 overall rank ratio for ground-truth hypotheses, and inter-expert consistency of 0.438/0.854. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting gains. Table 10 reassigns 3.765/2.730 from 'w/o mutation & recombination' to 'w/o multi-step', whose v1 values were 3.588/2.452, and adds joint-removal values of 2.863/2.578. Full-system GPT-4o scores and original expert outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The background/inspiration assumption, probability factorization, Markov-style approximation and ranking definition are mathematically retained. The full derivation in v1 Appendix A.1, Equations 5-19, corresponds to v4 Equations 4-18. Main-text compression and expanded explanations do not introduce a new proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central rediscovery claim, framework contribution and benchmark remain. A new introduction contribution list explicitly claims the first mathematical decomposition and first such Nature/Science-level chemistry rediscovery, adding priority claims for work already described in v1. Explicit materials-science wording does not establish new research coverage.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning retrieval's scaling plateau, why significance feedback can reduce reference matching, and possible reasons published hypotheses rank poorly. Appendix A.10 newly frames hypothesis discovery as exploiting hallucination, while A.15 interprets expert agreement as evidence of reliability. These substantially expand mechanism discussions and evaluation qualifications; the warning that low Matched Score need not imply poor quality already existed.

D1.justification: v4 specifies three benchmark annotators, cites the source papers for the four retained cases, documents reuse of the same prompt and hypotheses for additional evaluators, and explains third-expert sampling. The code/benchmark access link, existing scoring prompts, corpus-construction instructions and core search defaults remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantive positioning against Swanson linking and literature-based discovery in Appendix A.1, and against retrieval-augmented generation and self-consistency in A.11. These comparisons connect the central assumption and evolutionary component to additional research traditions. Kumar et al., Luo et al. and the retained cases' source papers are also newly cited.

P1.justification: v4 adds a contribution summary, introduces TOMATO-Chem and EU terminology, shortens the main derivation, and moves the main case study and background-option discussion into the appendix. Most existing exposition remains closely matched, with local copyediting rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v4 adds an input/output overview figure and extensive tabular displays for model comparisons, alternative evaluators, component analyses, ranking and inter-expert agreement. It also reverses retrieval-table column order, relocates the background ablation and supplies an expanded Q2 table. Figure 1 and many original table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Additional LLM evaluators and inter-expert checking strengthen the empirical assessment, while the ground-truth ranking test makes a practical limitation more concrete. These gains are limited by unexplained ablation reassignment in Table 10 and differing scoring descriptions in Table 6 and the unchanged appendix prompt. Section 6.2 also newly claims lower Average MS than MOOSE despite Table 10 showing 2.564 versus 2.464. Overall, validation improves, but reporting inconsistencies prevent a stronger quality judgment.
